tasks.notes: Q-031 and ADR-0024 lock the Central Rockies canonical path, Northern Plains alternative, Southern I-40 alternative, historical reference addresses, and public-road endpoint policy. On 2026-08-03 the first acquisition stage checksum-locked 15,525 unique NHPN route-family candidates across all 12 NHPN-backed policy segments, including all three signed-route slots and stable per-page canonical response hashes; the 54.43 MB raw response cache remains ignored. The second slice locked all 12 non-endpoint transfer anchors against exact NHPN OBJECTIDs and page-response hashes, with paired facilities reconciling within 24.401 meters, and added a cache-independent scripts/validate-continental-route.sh gate. Exact connected westbound NHPN edges, authored connector bounds, and dependent 3DEP products remain open before authoritative distance or geometry can be derived. Route semantics, reconstruction exceptions, packages, bot traversal, and human completion also remain open. P0-021 must still add scripts/run-continental-scenario.sh. The first graph is westbound only. On 2026-08-13 the owner set P0-021 as the next highest priority. The immediate gaps are the missing runtime layer (src/Cannonball.Core/Routes/Continental/, src/Cannonball.Core/Content/Continental/, game/World/Continental/, game/Automation/ContinentalRouteScenario.cs, scripts/run-continental-scenario.sh) and the connected westbound NHPN edge and 3DEP acquisition those depend on; none of them exist yet. On 2026-08-13 the NHPN endpoint snapping and connectivity audit, the second of the three requirements the candidate lock declares for exact-westbound-path-solve, completed offline from the checksum-locked cache. Six of twelve segments have an undirected path between their locked transfer nodes and six do not. Neither result is a westbound selection and the artifact does not claim one: a shortest undirected traversal can cross between opposing carriageways, so the lock records westbound_selection_validated false and the validator rejects any claim of a validated direction. Two transfer anchors snap hundreds of metres from any graph node, so the directed selection must also handle anchors that do not sit on the selected carriageway. No authoritative distance is claimed. The declared tolerance is enforced as a lock invariant rather than self-declared: derivation refuses a wider one and validation rejects a lock that claims it, so a widened tolerance cannot validate itself. Validation also rejects a lock claiming a validated westbound selection or a non-standard anchor limit, and a locked transfer anchor farther than 25 m from any candidate endpoint fails its segment rather than being reported as connectivity. scripts/validate-continental-route.sh now runs the edge-path validation, so the documented gate cannot pass while the artifact is unchecked. On 2026-08-14 that audit's central finding was corrected: the claim that NHPN carries these Interstates as paired directional carriageways was withdrawn as an artefact of grouping records by an LRS section extent rather than a per-record extent. Each segment is in fact a near-linear chain, 97 to 100 percent of whose endpoints join exactly two records, and the components arise from a small number of endpoint discontinuities of 1.0 to 661 m. The next stage therefore does not need a carriageway rule; it needs an evidenced decision per break about whether it may be bridged, which ADR-0018 forbids doing silently. A follow-up the same day corrected that correction's explanation of the breaks. Adjacency was inferred from the distance between nearby chain ends, but proximity is not adjacency: on i70 the two ends 5.82 m apart are at mileposts 280.4 and 4.9 of one section. Testing adjacency properly, one record's END_POINT against another's BEGIN_POIN on the same LRSKEY, only 3 of 67 chain ends across the twelve segments are contiguous. The candidate set therefore lacks the records that would join the chains rather than containing misaligned ones, so the next stage is a question about the acquisition predicate, possibly requiring re-acquisition, not a bridging policy. No bridging is performed and ADR-0018 still forbids inventing connectivity. On 2026-08-14 an owner-reported ride-height oscillation was traced to the road profile rather than the suspension: bounce frequency scales linearly with speed at a fixed ~50 m wavelength, where suspension resonance would sit at 1.71 Hz regardless. The road follows bare-earth terrain, whose short-wavelength relief is 94.1 mm RMS along the route, with no vertical-curve grading; the in-game road carries 41.7 mm RMS in the same band. Elevation sampling was additionally found to use nearest neighbour rather than interpolation and is now bilinear, which is a fidelity fix worth 12 percent of ride-height variation but not the cause of the symptom. Grading the profile is a route-geometry policy decision under ADR-0017 and ADR-0024 and is not taken here. The interpolation change alters every elevation value, so all route package hashes change. A grade-smoothing prototype now exists behind --grade-smoothing-meters, disabled by default and byte-identical to the shipped package when off. Measured at 40 m/s on the representative corridor, a 100 m window removes 64 percent of the ride-height variation for 3.8 cm mean departure from surveyed ground, and a 200 m window removes 78 percent for 7.5 cm. Choosing whether and how much to grade remains an owner decision under ADR-0017 and ADR-0024, including whether a graded profile may alter the authoritative route distance. On 2026-08-14 the owner selected the 100 m grading window from the two measured alternatives, and it now ships by default as pipeline.GRADE_SMOOTHING_METERS; passing 0 still reproduces the ungraded profile. Building the representative corridor with the new default reproduces route-v5-e6d2d877ddc5c52f byte for byte, the exact package the prototype measured at 100 m, so the 64 percent ride-height reduction carries over without a repeat capture, and disabling grading reproduces the previously shipped route-v5-c66ac9eeae94346a. The prototype's departure figures were corrected in the process: 3.8 cm mean and 17.1 cm max measured departure from the already-conditioned profile rather than from surveyed ground. Measured against the 3DEP raster at all 1,011 stations, the previously shipped ungraded package already departs 12.58 cm mean and 7.36 m max because of the spike median and the 7 percent grade projection, and grading adds 1.95 cm to the mean while reducing the maximum by 35 cm. Whether that pre-existing conditioning is correct was not examined and remains open. ADR-0017's question about whether a graded profile may alter the authoritative route distance is answered no and enforced: route distance is planimetric, and a test asserts edge lengths and every sample station are identical between graded and ungraded builds. On 2026-08-16 the contiguity finding was qualified rather than withdrawn. Measuring contiguity as a union of milepost intervals rather than by differencing sorted neighbours shows 320 of 377 segment and LRS key groups are already a single contiguous span, and the 104 remaining gaps are bimodal. Thirty-two are exactly one milepost quantum, 0.001 mile or 1.61 m, which is the finest distance NHPN can express because it publishes record mileposts to three decimals; about 40 percent of gaps sit at or near that precision. Two records that abut exactly can still be recorded a quantum apart, and an exact-equality adjacency test always rejects them, which is also the 1.0 m end of the 1.0 to 661 m endpoint discontinuity range the earlier connectivity audit reported. The interval-union method was necessary because the candidate set contains 38 exact duplicate records and many overlapping ones, which neighbour differencing reports as breaks; on i76-big-springs-to-denver the same overlapping pair appeared twice as an identical -58.634 mile gap. The remaining 45 gaps are over a mile, the largest 310 miles, and are not explained here; resolving whether they are a predicate miss, a route whose middle leaves the segment's states, or a key carrying only part of a route requires querying NHPN for that range without the sign filter, which is an acquisition and is not made. The scope limit is that this characterises adjacency within an LRS key only, since mileposts are key-local and say nothing about continuity where a route crosses between keys, which remains the geometric question the original endpoint-connectivity audit measured. No bridging is performed, no adjacency test is changed, and no lock is altered; a tolerance derived from the source quantum rather than chosen is now available to whoever makes that lock-affecting decision. Also on 2026-08-16 the 7.36 m worst-case departure from surveyed ground, recorded but not examined when the grading window shipped, was decomposed by conditioning stage. The 7 percent Lipschitz grade projection contributes nothing to the maximum: median alone and median plus projection both give 7.36 m, and the projection adds 0.41 cm to the mean. The whole worst case is the spike median, and what it removes is not road. At the worst station the raw 3DEP profile rises and falls 7.7 m over about 60 m at grades of 12.9 to 17.5 percent, and every other large departure has the same shape with steepest raw grades between 11.9 and 26.3 percent. US interstate design tops out near 6 to 7 percent, which is where the conditioning ceiling comes from, so those features are structures the surface model captured beside or above the centreline rather than the road surface, which is the case the conditioning docstring names. What that establishes is bounded: the median causes the whole maximum departure and the raw profile there is not road surface. What the features are is not established, since grade alone does not separate a structure from a laterally offset centreline sampling a cut bank, from vegetation in a surface model, or from a raster artefact; nor is it established that the elevation the median substitutes is the correct road elevation. Settling either needs a structure inventory such as the National Bridge Inventory or a bare-earth model compared against the surface model, both acquisitions under ADR-0018 and neither made. Two filter behaviours found while measuring are now pinned by tests: a median shifts near a spike on a slope, and at the corridor ends where the window is truncated, both by up to radius times spacing times grade, which is why station 100.0 m shows a 4.37 m departure near the corridor start. Left open: the 12.17 cm mean departure is not accounted for, and whether a 9-sample window is the right width is untouched. On 2026-08-27 the large-gap probe the milepost characterisation prescribed was made: a new probe-continental-milepost-gaps command fetched every over-a-mile gap's whole LRS key from NHPN without the sign or state filter, against a live service whose metadata hash still matches the lock, after regenerating the locked response cache from the live service and reproducing the committed lock's page hashes and 15,525-candidate union exactly. Zero records match the acquisition predicate while absent from the lock, so the acquisition was complete for what its predicate describes. Thirty-seven of the 45 gaps, 2,400.9 miles of milepost space, contain no NHPN records at all under any sign or state; the eight populated gaps decompose into records already locked under a neighbouring segment on a shared key, concurrency sections signed with a different route (the New Jersey Turnpike's I-95/NJ-700 sections, Ohio S-11), Montana I-15 beyond the corridor, and unrelated routes on colliding keys (Delaware S-15/S-896 on an I-15 key, Nebraska S-70 on an I-70 key), which also establishes that LRSKEY is not nationally unique. Regrouping the locked records by (STFIPS, LRSKEY) dissolves only one of the 45 large gaps (the New-Jersey-plus-Iowa composite on 000000008000153), so cross-state key reuse explains almost none of them. The 2026-08-14 predicate question is closed: no re-acquisition against these keys' milepost ranges can join the chains, because within-key mileposts end where the key stops carrying the route, and continuity across key boundaries is geometric. The next stage is a spatial probe at the six unconnected segments' actual break locations, without the sign filter, to establish whether the source asserts any joining feature there (an unsigned concurrency lives on a different key and is invisible to the milepost lens) or whether each break is authoring noise beyond the 1 m tolerance; that evidence is what an ADR-0018-compliant per-break decision needs. No lock was changed and the probe's responses stay in the ignored cache. On 2026-08-30 two independently built spatial probes landed and are reconciled in the 2026-08-30 audits. The geometric probe (probe-continental-geometric-breaks) chose 14 bounded sites - a minimum spanning tree over component pairs plus the two transfer-anchor mismatches - queried each with an unfiltered 250 m-padded envelope, and found a local undirected source path at 5 of 14 sites, every path using OBJECTIDs absent from the candidate lock (U-189 Utah, S-95 Arizona, unsigned Tennessee record 218838, I-270/U-36 Denver, and a 22-record S-10/U-101 Los Angeles path); Q-034 records the per-site ADR-0018 disposition those facts now require. The complementary break-end census (probe-continental-break-ends, sharing the snapped-graph builder and envelope helper) probed 500 m unfiltered windows around all 31 break ends - every degree-1 chain end except, per anchor, the chain end of that anchor's component farthest from the opposite anchor, which is the corridor continuing beyond the segment. It found that the chains do not dangle: at 25 of 31 break ends NHPN authors an exact shared-coordinate endpoint join (all 30 joins offset 0.0 m) with a record outside the candidate lock, naming joining OBJECTIDs at four of the geometric probe's nine no-path sites as well as at its five path sites. The Quad Cities 9.19 m milepost-contiguous pair is joined end-for-end by I-74/I-280 records 229625/229626 even though no local source path exists, so the joining pavement itself carries a discontinuity; the Rifle 320 m break joins US-6 exactly on its east side only; spur and fragment ends join I-84, I-270, I-275, I-294, US-6, US-22, historic US-66, an NJ-139-key record, and unsigned records. The census also grades joining geometry for the Q-034 corridor-fit review: the Memphis unsigned join is aligned within 3 degrees while the Topock S-95 joins meet at about 88 degrees, a tee rather than a continuation. Both probes agree the Omaha 1.011 m milepost-contiguous pair is joined by nothing and that the mainline is void at the Albuquerque I-40/I-25 gap, the I-78 Delaware River crossing, and the downtown Los Angeles gaps; the four pair interiors wider than the census windows (about 10.5 km in total) are the only NHPN evidence still ungathered. Neither probe bridges anything or changes any lock, and both leave their responses in ignored caches. On 2026-08-31 the Q-034 per-site disposition landed with its two missing evidence inputs gathered first. A new probe-continental-gap-interiors command swept the four break-pair interiors wider than the census windows (10.5 km; 23 unfiltered tiled windows; break-end selection and cross-component pairing factored into helpers shared with the census so the artifacts cannot disagree): the Albuquerque Big-I interior carries zero on-axis NHPN records (only frontage roads 300+ m off the chord), the Delaware River interior carries only S-611/unsigned crossing records with a zero-feature mid-river window, and the two downtown Los Angeles interiors carry the I-5/US-101/S-60/S-10 downtown tangle rather than clean I-10 mainline on the chord. A new probe-continental-nhs-breaks command adds ADR-0026 NHS acquisition capability (catalog URL-allowlist enforcement, service identity and public-domain-text validation, optional expected-metadata drift refusal, and the exact NHPN paging/checkpoint/page-hash discipline) and probed all 14 bounded sites plus the four interiors: NHS carries the declared route with continuous state-LRS measures and zero measure gap at every site, including every NHPN void (I-15 0015PM 244.838-265.59 across the 27.3 km fragment span, NM I40P through the Big-I, CO 070A across Rifle as a single feature, PA I-78 0.0-2.669 across the Delaware River). Both probes replayed semantically identically from checkpoints; zero retries; responses stay in ignored caches. The dispositions are recorded in the new validated artifact data/routes/continental/break-disposition.v1.json (status dispositions_recorded_lock_revision_pending, validated by validate-continental-break-dispositions inside scripts/validate-continental-route.sh, which enforces input-hash pins, full unconnected-segment coverage, the already-locked-OBJECTID exclusion, and a 30 m bounded-exception ceiling): 3 NHPN scoped-acquisition candidates (43839+43841 U-189 Payson, 218838 unsigned Memphis, 59709 I-270/U-36 Denver), 5 NHS fills, 2 bounded ADR-0018 authoring micro-gap exceptions (Omaha 1.011 m, Quad Cities 9.190 m, boundaries pinned to the probed end coordinates), and 4 ambiguous sites recorded as Q-034a-d sub-items (downtown LA mainline record review, the Topock ~88 degree tee mechanism, and both transfer-anchor mismatches). All 31 census break ends are reconciled in the record's census_ends section. No lock was modified, nothing was bridged, no direction was selected, and the 1 m tolerance is unchanged; see docs/audits/p0-021/2026-08-31-per-site-disposition.md. On 2026-08-31 the lock revision landed as one coherent change (see docs/audits/p0-021/2026-08-31-lock-revision.md). The candidate lock gained a validated supplementary_acquisitions section (acquire-continental-nhpn-supplements): 28 records across the 5 scoped sites - 43839+43841 U-189 Payson, 218838 unsigned Memphis, 59709 I-270/U-36 Denver, 38597 Topock junction sliver, and the 23-record downtown Los Angeles S-10/US-101 concurrency set - acquired with exact OBJECTID predicates, page hashes, checkpoint caches, and refusal of any live-metadata drift from the locked snapshot; the twelve 2026-08-04 segment snapshots are byte-identical and the union grew 15,525 to 15,553. Q-034a was resolved by the prescribed directed whole-key milepost review: the S-10 key's milepost space jumps one source quantum (16.239 to 16.24) across 2,112.6 m of the signed I-10/US-101 downtown concurrency, and the unique exact-join 23-record set (9 S-10 + 14 US-101) was acquired, connecting i10-ontario-to-i405 end-to-end in pure NHPN (54.41 mi). Q-034b was resolved by sliver geometry: 38597 (S-95 key, mp 0-0.015, 14.1 m) spans the Topock gap exactly with 0.0 m endpoint and line offsets at both ends - the corridor's own junction pavement, so NHS fill and bounded exception were rejected. The five NHS fills are locked in data/routes/continental/nhs-fill-lock.v1.json (acquire-continental-nhs-fills, validated by validate-continental-nhs-fills inside scripts/validate-continental-route.sh): catalog URL-allowlist enforcement, NHS service identity and public-domain validation, expected-metadata drift refusal (live hash a29f96df... matched the disposition evidence exactly), full paging/checkpoint/page-hash discipline, ADR-0026 dual NHPN/NHS ancestry, per-record YEAR/VERSION/UPDATE_DAT (all 2020), and zero state-LRS measure gap at every site. Transfer and edge-path locks were re-derived against the revised candidate set: all 12 anchors byte-identical; 8 of 12 segments now carry an undirected NHPN path between their anchors (was 6; +i10 54.41 mi, +i15 174.949 mi - the Payson acquisition alone connected i15, proving the 27.3 km pairing was fragment isolation, not a mainline break), and the fill lock's chain_connectivity section records that 10 of 12 segments chain end-to-end once the locked fills bridge their pinned break ends (i40 2,091.83 mi with the 1,854 m Big-I chord, i70 499.94 mi with the 320 m Rifle chord); 4,594.5 mi of corridor is now continuously locked or chained (was 1,773.4). Chain lengths are mixed-ancestry undirected chains, not a westbound selection and not an authoritative distance. The disposition record moved to status lock_revision_implemented_sub_items_pending with pins to the revised artifacts and the fill lock, and its validator now proves implementation (every scoped site matched by a supplement with exactly its OBJECTIDs, every nhs_fill site by a fill-lock site). Q-034c/d stay open with their mechanism space halved: the measure review proved no record endpoint, locked or unlocked, lies within the 25 m anchor limit of either mismatched anchor (both anchors sit mid-record on their own locked pavement at 381.157 m and 253.027 m from the nearest endpoint), ruling out approach-record acquisition; the remaining mechanisms are anchor re-derivation or an edge-split-at-anchor solve. Replay: both acquisition commands resume every page from checkpoints and reproduce the revised locks exactly modulo acquisition timestamps; transfer and edge derivations reproduce their digests exactly. The two ADR-0018 micro-gap overlays remain un-authored, waiting for the reconstruction gates; the 1 m tolerance and 25 m anchor limit are unchanged. On 2026-08-31 the topology closure landed (docs/audits/p0-021/2026-08-31-topology-closure.md). Q-034c/d were resolved by adopting edge-split-at-anchor: the edge-path solve resolves an anchor through endpoint snapping first and, only beyond the unchanged 25 m anchor limit, splits the deterministically nearest locked record's edge at the anchor's projection, recording the split machine-checkably (anchor_edge_splits; part_range_m on any solved sub-edge). Both anchors resolved at 0.000 m offset (i78: 433412 Holland Tunnel, split 381.157 m along its 1,576.081 m part; i80: 431704, split 253.027 m along 742.918 m); the ADR-0024 transfer lock is byte-identical, the ten endpoint-anchored segments' solve entries are unchanged, and anchor re-derivation was rejected for moving research-grounded transfer coordinates 381/253 m onto NHPN segmentation artifacts. The ADR-0018 reconstruction gates now exist: author-continental-reconstruction-overlays authors each bounded_reconstruction_exception as a chord overlay between the disposition's pinned boundary coordinates, accepted only when the endpoint-position (1 m), length-bound (pinned agreement plus the 30 m ceiling), source-adjacency (milepost contiguity on a shared LRS key), and self-intersection gates all pass, refusing with machine-readable diagnostics otherwise; curvature/grade/sightline/collision/lane/drivability gates are recorded as explicitly deferred to the reconstruction-geometry stage, and the adjoining end tangents are recorded as that stage's authoring constraint. The two overlays are authored in data/routes/continental/reconstruction-overlay-lock.v1.json with full evidence chains, page-hash provenance, and content-addressed digests, validated cache-independently by validate-continental-reconstruction-overlays inside scripts/validate-continental-route.sh (now six stages). The gates demonstrably reject: the first Quad Cities run was refused by a draft straight-through heading gate that inspection proved wrong for a gap sitting on the I-80/I-74 interchange corner of I-80's own LRS (77.2 degrees between end tangents, now recorded as the geometry-stage constraint). 12 of 12 segments now chain anchor-to-anchor (was 8 pure-NHPN / 10 with fills): +i78 143.6 mi (fills plus the Q-034c split), +i80 1,556.0 mi (fills stage blocked only by the exceptions until the overlays bridge them); 6,294.1 mi of corridor is continuously locked or chained (was 4,594.5). Chains remain undirected and mixed-ancestry - no westbound selection and no authoritative distance. The disposition record closed to lock_revision_implemented_topology_closed (no ambiguous site may remain; anchor splits and overlays are cross-checked by validator), and Q-034 moved to Recently resolved. Replay is exact for every revised lock (regenerated caches, checkpoint resumption, identical digests). Next bounded slice: the NHPN-NHS conflation model over the five locked fill spans and the 3DEP product lock over the closed corridor - the inputs the reconstruction-geometry stage needs before the westbound directed selection; then reconstruction geometry (including the deferred gates at the two overlay sites), the runtime layer, and the human gates.

tasks.title: Layered deterministic highway traffic director
acceptance: A deterministic macro flow and spawn schedule resolves into bounded near-player traffic before it becomes relevant and reconstructs identically after save/resume
Same-direction agents occupy only legal lanes on the active directed edge; opposing agents occupy only the validated reciprocal carriageway and never share the player's lane ribbon
Density, composition, speed distributions, lane intent, indicators, merges, exits, entrances, transfers, incidents, and gap acceptance remain readable at the declared high-speed target
Far traffic uses pooled or instanced representations and only near traffic receives physics, with measured update, memory, tunneling, and collision-substep budgets
Traffic survives streaming, branch prewarm/eviction, local-origin rebases, route changes, compression modes, and exact save/resume without teleporting into unsafe sightlines
Adversarial scenarios cover missing carriageway pairs, ramps, lane drops, interchanges, stopped vehicles, maximum closing speed, degraded quality, and deterministic replay

tasks.notes: Q-021 was resolved by the owner on 2026-07-23: production scenery pursues grounded realism for every traversed state with route-specific subregion profiles where the real environment changes; Colorado remains the representative technical slice rather than the coast-to-coast art template. Q-022 selected a Ryzen 9 5900X / RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB / 64 GB Windows 11 PC, then selected 2560x1440 High at a stable 60 FPS and layered measurement-driven budgets as the first production reference. Provisional gates require p95 presented-frame time at or below 16.67 ms, p99 at or below 20 ms, no steady-driving stall above 50 ms after warm-up, GPU memory at or below 9.5 GB, process working set at or below 16 GB, and no sustained positive growth over a 30-minute steady-state run. On 2026-07-26 the owner selected an owner-started Codex session running directly on the Windows reference PC and native RTX 3080 Ti renderer, using a persistent pinned toolchain and reusable caches but a fresh clean Git worktree at the exact reviewed commit for every capture. Evidence records tool versions, worktree cleanliness, and input hashes; no standing remote access or stored credentials are authorized. Representative production captures and derived scene, subsystem, streaming, memory, and content-class allocations remain open for ratification. Runtime integration owns only collision-free environment siblings, environment scenario flags, scenario-script routing, continuous terrain ribbons outside the authoritative road margin, and measured environment geometry budgets; authoritative road elevation, road collision, and vehicle physics remain outside this task. On 2026-07-30 ownership expanded narrowly to the shared M0 workflow, aggregate test runner, integrated scenario, focused gate, audit, and owner handoff needed to prove that the existing Hero GT, production road, and balanced regional environment contracts coexist in one moving official-engine runtime. This machine integration evidence does not promote the current procedural baselines to production art or close any human, rights, or Q-022 performance gate. P1-013 owns the Q-022 capture harness, target-profile recapture, evidence gaps, and budget-ratification state; this task consumes only ratified budgets and does not advance its art, rights, or readability gates from P1-013 baseline evidence. On 2026-08-14 verify-environment-assets.sh was found red on main. Its shell assertion demands max_terrain_seam_m be exactly 0.0000 while the runtime contract fails only above 0.05 m and the scenario reports 0.0005 m. The seam is measured on float32 world coordinates, whose representable spacing is 0.488 mm at 5 km against a 24,665 m corridor, so exact zero is unreachable beyond roughly two kilometres from the origin regardless of geometry. Pre-existing: the same value is reported before and after the elevation interpolation change. Whether to assert the declared ceiling instead, or to measure the seam in a rebased frame, is P1-010's specification decision and is not taken here. On 2026-08-14 the owner set the terrain seam specification: the gate asserts the seam is within what float32 can represent at the vertices being compared, rather than an exact 0.0000 metres that is unreachable in principle beyond roughly two kilometres from the origin. Implementing the option as it was put, at one unit in the last place, still failed at 1.155, so every seam pair was measured instead of widening the ceiling to fit. All sixteen pairs are exact integer multiples of the float32 spacing at their own magnitude, between zero and five and never a fraction, which demonstrates rather than infers that the seam is representation and not authored geometry. The ceiling is five units per component because adjacent chunks derive the shared boundary vertex through their own anchors and each pays five float32 roundings, enumerated beside TerrainSeamRoundingSteps in WorldStreamer. The observed worst pair sits at 5.00 against a ceiling of 8.66. The root cause is the double derivation: computing the boundary vertex once and sharing it would make it bit-identical and the original assertion reachable at any distance. That is a change to how the terrain ribbon is framed, carries visual risk, and is not attempted. verify-environment-assets.sh now passes on all four quality profiles, having previously failed silently because grep -q under set -e exits without a message. On 2026-08-14 the Godot resource wrappers that leak at engine shutdown were released. A failing Linux M0 run listed 78 leaked unsafe references across 11 types, dominated by 26 ArrayMesh, 15 StandardMaterial3D and 10 BoxMesh, all from one cause: a resource wrapper built inline in a node initializer is dropped when the initializer completes, so nothing disposes it and it survives to finalisation after the engine has torn down. RoadChunk and JunctionSeam record 17 such constructions through Owned() and release them from the predelete handler they already had, RegionalEnvironmentChunk takes ownership of the terrain ribbon mesh handed to it, both visual kits became IDisposable discovering their resources by reflection so a newly added one cannot escape, and WorldStreamer disposes them at predelete. Kit-owned materials referenced by chunks are deliberately not wrapped, since releasing them from a chunk would leave the kit holding a disposed wrapper. Nothing rendering is affected because the node holds its own reference; verify-environment-assets.sh passes on all four quality profiles with identical triangle counts. The claim is deliberately narrow: this removes undisposed wrappers of exactly the types the failing run named, which is inspectable, while whether it ends the intermittent segfault is not demonstrable from one green run, because main's most recent Linux M0 also recorded zero leaks and passed. The same PR deflaked test_chase_camera_damps_vehicle_yaw_and_keeps_a_level_horizon, which failed on Windows CI having held full throttle for about 0.12 seconds of its 7 second budget: one deadline covered both input latency and vehicle acceleration, so the first could consume the second and the test asserted something about the runner. They are now budgeted separately with acceleration timed from when throttle engages. No assertion was weakened. A gap noticed and not addressed: scripts/verify-road-assets.sh calls rg, which is not present in this environment, so it fails locally with command not found; it is not part of the M0 gate.

tasks.notes: The clean Release baseline at revision 5a42ecef4af6f90fe616fceae1e69309471d200e is reproducible but used the balanced environment profile. On 2026-08-13 the required High content-profile recapture completed at revision de42c82fdd6519895b9164c6d8a11a4f08bd7015 from a fresh clean worktree: nine sequential scenarios at 2560x1440 Release Forward+ on the native RTX 3080 Ti. Eight used the high environment profile (48/18/10 instances per chunk, terrain stride 1); degraded-quality deliberately retained the low profile as the degraded comparison point. This closes the High content-profile gap only; the repository still defines no High renderer preset. Frame-time percentiles, GPU memory, and working set pass with 8.6x p95 and 6.7x p99 headroom. The 30-minute run passes the proposed sustained-growth operationalization at 0.56 MiB/min with R-squared 0.16, but Q-022d has not ratified that slope and R-squared rule, so it is not a pass against an owner-ratified criterion. The ratified zero-stall limit fails in four scenarios across 12 steady-driving events; three streaming runs with identical arguments produced 4, 0 and 0 events, so the failure is intermittent and no rate is claimed. Every event reports render CPU plus GPU near 1 ms and the streaming counters do not separate stalling from clean runs, so the cause remains unattributed and Q-022c still owns how attribution is obtained. Raising balanced to high did not measurably raise percentile frame time, so neither capture can price environment density and the proposed layer-2 allocations remain underivable from measurement. A V-Sync-on presentation check now exists and passed, but it locked to the 120 Hz reference display rather than the 60 FPS target presentation. One streaming stall classification is flagged for review because its surrounding state matches post-loop-wrap re-acquisition; excluding it changes no verdict. P1-013 remains in progress: traffic and weather coverage, per-subsystem attribution, a repository-defined High renderer preset, and owner ratification are still open. The owner answered Q-022a on 2026-08-13 by choosing instrumentation over further repetition. The harness now attaches per-frame GC generation counts, streamer build/removal/rebase/failure/chunk-count deltas, and engine process timings to every recorded stall, with run-level coincidence totals. Its first observed stall coincided with a Gen0 and Gen1 collection and no streaming work; that is one sample and records coincidence, not cause. A second run of the same nine scenarios at identical arguments on 2026-08-13 recorded zero steady-driving stalls against the first run's twelve, eleven hours apart on the same machine and content. The instrumentation captured no attribution data because there was nothing to attribute. The failure is therefore not reproducible. That is consistent with a machine-state, contention, or measurement-method cause but excludes none, including an intermittent content, code, driver, or instrumentation cause, which need not appear in any given matrix; the first run's events remain real measurements and are not withdrawn. One repeat run showed mean render GPU time about ten times its siblings at identical arguments, showing that a capture's GPU timing can change by an order of magnitude on a metric the workspace policy does not observe. The capture front door now exposes --max-fps and records the machine's own GPU utilisation, clock, temperature, power draw, and GPU-context process list before and after every run; the record enforces nothing because whether machine state should gate a capture is Q-022a. A 60 FPS engine frame-cap check closes the coverage gap Q-022e named; it is a frame cap, not a 60 Hz output mode. The build holds the cap at 60.009 mean FPS with about 2.7 ms mean render GPU time and zero stalls, but the run records p95_frame_ms as failed at 16.9075 ms. The 16.67 ms limit sits 3.3 microseconds above a 60 FPS cap period, so it is attainable in principle but permits only 3.3 microseconds of p95 jitter; measured jitter was about 241 microseconds, roughly 72 times that budget. That is a threshold-margin finding for owner decision under Q-022e, not an arithmetic impossibility and not a change to ADR-0023. On 2026-08-14 the owner answered Q-022a, Q-022b, Q-022d and Q-022e; ADR-0023 gained a ratification addendum and all four are recorded closed in the handoff document. Q-022c remains the only Q-022 question open. Q-022a option A2: the capture front door now refuses to publish a capture that did not start idle or that saw a new GPU client arrive mid-measurement, with --allow-contended to record one deliberately. Two corrections came out of running it rather than reasoning about it. GPU memory utilisation was in the first criterion and had to be removed, because it measures the fraction of the sample period in which device memory was accessed rather than contention and an idle compositor holds it in the mid teens, so it refused every capture on an interactive machine. And a bounded settle wait was needed because a capture immediately after another was refused at 11 percent, which would have measured recency rather than idleness and refused most of a nine-scenario matrix. Sampling now runs throughout the measurement at 2 second intervals rather than only bracketing it, because the run that motivated this would not have been caught by brackets. A recorded limit: nvidia-smi reports 35 clients at idle on this machine and does not list the capture itself, since Godot is a graphics rather than compute client, so the during-run test can detect a new client but cannot attribute one. The zero-stall threshold is not declared passed by any of this and remains failed until a matrix satisfying the precondition records no stall. Q-022b option A: layer 2 stays unmeasured reserves and nothing gates on it, while layer-3 content-class caps are unaffected. Q-022d ratified: slope above 1 MiB per minute AND R squared at or above 0.5, and criterion_status in the emitted acceptance changes from proposed to ratified, so growth statements now mean a ratified requirement was met. Q-022e: a frame-capped run is judged on cap adherence, mean FPS within 0.1 of the cap and p50 within 0.1 ms of the cap period with no stall over 50 ms, and the 16.67 ms p95 limit is not applicable to it. Both paths were verified by real captures: uncapped reports p95 PASS and cap_adherence NOT_APPLICABLE, while a 60 FPS capped run reports p95 NOT_APPLICABLE at the same 16.9025 ms that the previous rule marked failed, and cap_adherence PASS at 60.039 mean FPS with a 16.6575 ms p50. The passed key is omitted entirely from a non-applicable entry rather than set true, so a consumer that does not check applicable cannot report a limit as passed that was never evaluated. P1-013 still cannot complete: ADR-0023 requires representative traffic and weather content before production budgets are ratified, and neither system exists. On 2026-08-14 the owner also decided the disposition of the briefly-published installed-application list: leave the unreferenced commit to expire rather than requesting a purge or rewriting history. The branch was deleted and main never carried it, so the commit is unreachable by ref and reachable only by SHA until garbage collection runs. The exposure is executable names of installed applications, not credentials or personal data. record_machine_state.py has retained only client counts since the leak was caught, and a test now asserts the client summary carries no process identifier, image path, or executable name, so the same mistake fails the suite rather than reaching a commit. On 2026-08-16 the owner answered Q-022c by choosing in-engine per-subsystem timers, closing the last open Q-022 question. Cannonball.Core.Performance.SubsystemProfiler times road, route context, environment, vehicle and UI at their own boundaries and reference captures report mean and worst-frame CPU per subsystem. Traffic, effects and lighting hold layer-2 reserves but have no implementation and are deliberately not instrumented, because timing a system that does not exist reports a confident zero. Two design points were forced by tracing rather than assumption: regions measure exclusive time because environment chunks build inside the streamer's road region through CompletePendingLoads and AttachChunk, and an earlier comment asserting they did not nest was wrong; and the profiler drains on read rather than resetting at frame start, because a reset would depend on Godot node processing order and silently discard the time of any subsystem processed earlier in the tree. The measurement confirms rather than overturns the Q-022b answer: across 90 seconds at 60 m/s the five instrumented subsystems used 0.069 ms of CPU per frame against a 2.09 ms mean frame, about 3 percent, so a ratified layer-2 millisecond split would partition 3 percent of the frame. Two limits are recorded: an in-process timer cannot separate a slow subsystem from a descheduled process, evidenced by one frame charging about 25 ms each to road, route context and vehicle, which is one suspension attributed to whichever region was open; and GPU time is not attributed at all, though the workload is GPU bound at 86 percent of frames. P1-013 still cannot complete, because ADR-0023 requires representative traffic and weather content before production budgets are ratified and neither system exists.

tasks.title: Exported builds apply the GC nursery setting at launch
tasks.scope: Make an exported desktop build start with the same .NET nursery size that scripts/godot.sh sets for repo-driven runs, so a player gets the frame pacing the reference captures measure.
acceptance: An exported build launched the way a player launches it runs with the ratified nursery size, demonstrated by a measurement from the exported build rather than from the editor or a script
The mechanism does not depend on scripts/godot.sh, which an exported build never runs
The chosen mechanism is recorded with why it works, given that System.GC.Gen0Size in a runtimeconfig template was measured to have no effect because Godot hosts the runtime itself
Every supported desktop target is covered, or the uncovered targets are named
A run of the exported build records gen0 collection count and worst frame time so the setting can be shown to be active rather than assumed
tasks.notes: Opened on 2026-08-16 from the frame-stutter root cause. Godot wrappers carry finalizers and cannot die in gen0, so every collection promotes and pause length tracks nursery size. Measured at 50 m/s over 60 s on the representative corridor, the dynamic default gave 9 collections with a 39.7 ms worst frame, 8 MB gave 17 collections with a 24.5 ms worst frame, and 64 MB gave 2 collections with a 116.5 ms worst frame, so more frequent smaller pauses win. scripts/godot.sh now exports DOTNET_GCgen0size=800000 hex, which covers check.sh, every scenario, every capture and every verify script. An exported build does not run that script and therefore does not get the setting, so a player would see the default behaviour the captures no longer measure. A runtimeconfig.template.json carrying System.GC.Gen0Size was tried first and removed: it merged into the generated Cannonball.runtimeconfig.json correctly and had no effect, confirmed because adding the environment variable on top still changed gen0 counts. Godot hosts the runtime itself, so the application's configProperties never reach GC initialisation. Leaving an inert setting in the tree would have looked authoritative while doing nothing. Candidate mechanisms not yet evaluated: a launcher shim or .bat/.sh wrapper that sets the variable before starting the binary, an export-time hook, or a Godot-side runtime setting if one exists that is honoured.
